Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract, then inspect the inherited rollout evidence and both wake views before touching the policy. I’ll also consult the fish-control bookshelf under the required transfer protocol and keep any adopted mechanism traceable in the notes.

The workspace requires one fixed-morphology candidate and explicitly forbids local CFD. `rg` is unavailable here, so I’m using `find` for inventory. The prefill is the weakest sampled result, so I’m treating the stronger examples as behavioral contrasts, not just copying the parent controller.

The textual evidence confirms direct uniform still water for every sample. The best prior is the bearing-trend curvature controller (25.85% normalized progress, 9.141L minimum distance), while the prefilled yaw-rate variant barely improves (3.66%, then recedes). I’m now reading their combined top-down/oblique sheets, plus the newer half-cycle rollout, to identify whether the failure is steering authority, thrust loss, or a sign/topology problem.

The wake sheets and inherited parent rollout agree on the mechanism boundary: both forms of tail-only half-cycle asymmetry preserve an alternating wake but still hook upward and exit around 9–12.6T; neither beats the static posterior-curvature parent’s 9.141L approach. That falsifies the prior “tail half-cycle alone will recover after crossing” hypothesis. I’m quantifying when bearing, yaw, slip, and actuator limits diverge so the next candidate changes the feedback channel rather than retuning the same one.

The quantitative cross-check shows why another half-cycle gain is a dead end: relative to the static best, opposition relief lowers mean absolute yaw rate (1.31→1.13 rad/T) and posterior speed-limit contact (5.8%→2.6%) yet still reaches bearing about −1.28 rad at the same upper exit and gives up 0.71L of closest approach. The stronger inherited asymmetry exits even earlier after only 11.655L. I’m recording a candidate hypothesis that instead uses target-relative lateral-slip damping to reverse steering before the visible upward drift compounds.

The candidate now preserves the strongest carrier and changes only the steering observation structure: bounded body-frame lateral velocity acts as a derivative residual on bearing, with no clock, coordinates, hidden state, or extra drive. I’m distilling the newly completed half-cycle evidence into durable guidance before running the contract checks.

The first mandated check exposed a workspace-metadata defect: `README.md` marks the same optimizer parent as “copied to guidance” twice, so the checker cannot identify exactly one assigned parent. I’m removing only that duplicate marker, leaving the parent identity and candidate evidence unchanged, then rerunning the check.

Guidance semantics and the solver edit boundary now pass. Julia is not installed in this environment, so the executable smoke command cannot run locally; I’m invoking the required check-runner to independently audit the policy contract, schema, bounds, and reflection behavior without CFD.

The required check-runner was invoked, but its pinned `gpt-5.4-mini` model is unavailable on this account, so it could not execute. I’m completing the same non-CFD audit directly: schema-reference equality, finite-output grid, steering bounds, reflection equivariance, and the already passing guidance/boundary checks.

The direct audit passes: all 10 referenced parameters are declared, 2,916 boundary-state combinations remain finite, steering curvature stays within 12°, reflection equivariance is exact to the test tolerance, and the solver boundary contains only the permitted policy edit. I’m doing the final artifact/line audit now; no CFD has been run.

Completed exactly one candidate:

- [candidate_target_policy.jl](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1) adds bounded body-frame lateral-slip damping to the strongest traveling-bend carrier.
- [wake_policy_notes.md](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1) records visual diagnosis, bookshelf transfer, and falsification criteria.
- [control_experience.md](guidance/control_experience.md:53) records the negative reusable result for tail-only half-cycle asymmetry.
- Removed a duplicated assigned-parent marker from `README.md` that initially broke the guidance checker.

Validation passed for guidance semantics, solver boundary, parameter schema, 2,916 finite state-grid cases, 12° curvature bound, and reflection equivariance. The required check-runner was invoked but its pinned model was unavailable; Julia was also unavailable. No CFD was run.
